stripe_api_calls_you_will_make._note: All calls go to https://api.stripe.com. Authenticate with: Authorization: Bearer $STRIPE_SECRET_KEY

step_A_look_up_or_create_customer._when: Every time create-checkout is called — find the user's existing Stripe Customer or create one

search_existing.on_result: If data array is non-empty, use data[0].id as the customer ID. If empty, go to create_new.

key_response_fields.id: The Stripe Customer ID (cus_...) — store this on your user record

create_new.on_result: Store the returned id (cus_...) on the user record in your DB. Use it for all future calls.

key_response_fields.url: The hosted Stripe checkout page URL — return this to the frontend
key_response_fields.id: Session ID (cs_...) — you can store this if needed

step_C_retrieve_subscription_in_webhook._when: Inside the checkout.session.completed webhook handler, after you get the subscription ID from the session object

key_response_fields.trial_end: Unix timestamp if on trial, null if not. Use this to decide whether to set user status = 'trialing' or 'active'.
key_response_fields.current_period_end: Unix timestamp for when the current billing period ends
key_response_fields.customer: Stripe Customer ID (cus_...) — should match what you already stored

step_C_retrieve_subscription_in_webhook.decision_logic: If subscription.trial_end is not null → set user status = 'trialing'. If null → set user status = 'active'.

what_to_do: 1. Look up or create a Stripe Customer for the authenticated user (see stripe_api_calls_you_will_make.step_A)
2. Store the Stripe Customer ID (cus_...) on the user record if it didn't exist yet
3. Create a Stripe Checkout Session (see stripe_api_calls_you_will_make.step_B) using the correct body for the plan
4. Return the session URL from the Stripe response

find_subscription.description: Returns the authenticated user's current subscription status. Frontend calls this immediately after Stripe redirects back to /dashboard?sub=success.

webhook.auth: None — verified by Stripe signature header instead

signature_verification.critical: Use the raw unparsed request body. Parsing JSON first breaks the signature check.

events_to_handle.action: Find user via event.data.object.metadata.user_id. Store stripe_customer_id and stripe_subscription_id on the user. Call GET /v1/subscriptions/:id (see stripe_api_calls_you_will_make.step_C) to check trial_end. If trial_end is not null set status = 'trialing', else 'active'.
Set status = 'active'. Update renewed_at to now.
Email user to update payment method. Set status = 'none' after grace period.
Fires 3 days before trial ends. Email user: trial ending in 3 days, they will be charged.
Fires when subscription status changes (e.g. trial → active). Sync status using the map below.

trial: 2. Backend creates/finds Stripe Customer, creates Checkout Session with trial_period_days:7
4. Frontend redirects browser to that URL — Stripe handles card capture
5. User enters card, NOT charged yet, trial starts
7. Frontend GETs subscription.find, stores status='trialing', user is in
pro: 2. Backend creates/finds Stripe Customer, creates Checkout Session (no trial)
4. Frontend redirects browser to that URL — Stripe handles payment
7. Frontend GETs subscription.find, stores status='active', user is in
cancel: User presses back/cancel on Stripe page → redirected to /choose-plan, nothing changed

what_frontend_has_already_done: Both plan buttons call createCheckoutSession('trial'|'pro') and redirect to result.url
On /dashboard?sub=success: calls subscription.find, syncs status to localStorage, hard-reloads to /dashboard
The proxy route already whitelists 'subscription.*' paths — no proxy changes needed
